lines.text: A fifty-year-old Asian woman complains of nocturia and dizziness. Her fasting glucose is three point nine, her sodium is low at one hundred and thirty-one, and her potassium is high at six point one. What is the likely diagnosis?
The answer is Addison’s disease.
This woman is dizzy, and she keeps getting up at night. That is nocturia.
The salt is pouring away. Her sodium is low, one hundred and thirty-one.
(laugh) And the potassium bananas pile up. Her potassium is high, six point one.
Add hypoglycaemia and hypotension, from a lack of mineralocorticoid and glucocorticoid.
The tired adrenals are tested with the short synACTHen test. An absent or impaired cortisol response confirms it.
Remember: low sodium, high potassium, and low glucose mean Addison's disease.

A sixty-year-old man complains of knee pain, and there is a moderate effusion. The fluid is withdrawn, and microscopy shows crystals that are positively birefringent under polarized light. What is the likely diagnosis?
The answer is pseudogout.
This sixty-year-old man has a painful knee.
The knee holds a moderate effusion.
The doctor withdraws the fluid, and the syringe is full of crystals.
(laugh) Look at the crystals, they are having a party in the joint!
Under polarized light, the crystals are positively birefringent.
Crystals in a joint cause synovitis. There are two main forms, gout and pseudogout. Gout is the more common.
Remember: positively birefringent crystals in a knee effusion mean pseudogout.

A twenty-one-year-old footballer has a stabbing pain above his right knee that came on suddenly while he was sprinting. He is unable to extend the leg, and walks with a limp. There is suprapatellar swelling and an absent knee jerk. What is the likely diagnosis?
The answer is a tear of the quadriceps tendon.
This twenty-one-year-old footballer feels a sudden stabbing pain while sprinting.
The pain is just above the knee, where the tendon has snapped.
There is suprapatellar swelling above the kneecap.
He cannot extend his leg, he limps, and the knee jerk is absent.
The quadriceps muscles in the front of the thigh are the principal extensors of the knee joint.
The mechanism of injury is inconsistent with a fractured patella.
Remember: sudden pain while sprinting, with no leg extension, means a quadriceps tendon tear.
